root_cause: The default division operator `/` in Python results in a floating-point number. In this context, the list `sorted_b` might be expected to contain integers. If the floating-point formatting impacts the intended sorting or representation, it needs correction.
suggestion:
Suggestion 1. Use Integer Division Change the division operator from `/` (floating-point division) to `//` (integer division):
```java
n, k = list(map(int, input().split()))
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
b = []
for i in range(n):
    if a[i] % k == 0:
        c = a[i] // k
        b.append(c)
sorted_b = sorted(b)
print(" ".join(map(str, sorted_b)))
```
This way, `c` will be an integer, ensuring `sorted_b` contains integers.
